inspiration: Monster stats are rolled from a per-type default: max HP gets base plus a random amount up to a range, current HP rolls from its own range when the ranges differ, and if the two ranges match current HP follows the max roll. HP is clamped to max afterwards (entity.cpp lines 20127-20157; defaults switch in stat_shared.cpp line 159). Row 7 and row 18 variance: same creature type, a few points different, roll-then-clamp order.

Items carry two names: an identified name and an unidentified one (item_names.json lines 5-6). Loot ceremony: a new drop shows its generic name until used or identified. Keep the two-name field; reveal with a colour and sound stinger, not text (row 18 and phone inspect).

Spell failure rises when the spell is less known: the more it is cast, the better it is known (types of spell failure.txt line 10). Failure types: mana overdraw costs health, a fizzle, a self-damage explosion, a summoned threat (lines 14-17). Row 13 specials: a learning-curve failure ladder the player can read.

A death opt-out zone: after death the player may enter a hard arena for a second life, or accept permanent loss (kill zone.txt line 1). Row 17 death and respawn: a loss made bearable by a risky second chance, with the choice shown up front.

A creature signature tied to a player state: a brute leaps and tackles when the player is levitating over a pit (minotaur.txt line 1). Row 7 creature behaviour and pit zones: trigger on a player state, telegraph the leap.

Numbered string tables with one entry per line, a number, a space, then the string, and '#' comments (lang/en.txt line 2). Locale-ready and easy to diff. For the catalogue (row 20 and 21): one numbered table per language, keys as numbers, not text.

briefs.label: Pit Tackler (own label)
briefs.why: A brute that waits for the player to be in a risky state (over a pit) and then leaps is readable at 375 wide: the leap is the telegraph, and the player's choice (cross or wait) is the fight.
briefs.keep: a trigger tied to the player's state; a leap that ends in a tackle; a readable wind-up before the leap
briefs.change: our brute is a bull-shaped creature with a glowing neck ring, not a minotaur design; our trigger is a bridge or ledge we author in zone data; the leap is a wind-up plus ground shadow, not a jump arc

briefs.label: Unlabelled Relic (own label)
briefs.why: An item that shows a generic name until identified makes each loot drop a small question, and the reveal is the reward.
briefs.keep: two names per item (generic until identified, real after); reveal by use
briefs.change: our reveal is a colour and sound stinger with a glyph-shape hint; the generic label is a shape, not a word; the item families are ours

briefs.label: Second Chance Arena (own label)
briefs.why: A death that offers a short, hard second life makes a loss feel like a choice, not a wall.
briefs.keep: death leads to a choice: a hard arena with a chance back, or permanent loss; the choice is shown before it is made
briefs.change: our arena is a timed duel against one champion from our roster; the afterlife is a shrine and a flicker of light, not the donor's wording; the chance back is a visible token, not a hidden roll
